title: AI scientist now running its own biology lab
key_facts: Chalmers University of Technology, University of Gothenburg and University of Cambridge built an AI scientist
It generates hypotheses, designs experiments, directs lab automation, analyses results and refines next experiments
Used a database of about 60,000 relationships and produced nearly 2,000 testable predictions
Found a glutamate and spermine-treated cells interaction and that aminoadipate may partly protect yeast from formic-acid stress
Published in the Journal of the Royal Society Interface
Humans still set boundaries and interpret findings
quote_evidence: The research has been published in the Journal of the Royal Society Interface.
the system is not a completely independent scientist working without humans.
These findings are important not because they immediately translate into a new medicine
why_it_matters_hint: First complete loop from question to lab test and learning in one AI system, in yeast only.
event_date: Published 5 Oct 2026; study date not stated
notes: Moneycontrol's own write-up of the study; underlying release not seen.
